newsitem.title: USA: DC council offers balanced budget to control panel.
newsitem.headline: DC council offers balanced budget to control panel.

text.p: The District of Columbia's Council on Tuesday cleared a $3.3 billion fiscal 1998 budget for the city that is designed to balance D.C.'s budget one year earlier than mandated by Congress and make significant changes in a budget proposed by D.C. Mayor Marion Barry.

The council's proposed budget, approved 9-2, now goes to the city's congressionally appointed financial control board for clearance. The five-member panel has until June 15 to send a final proposed budget to Capitol Hill for review.

"This budget discipline is important to the financial markets, and will enable us to get back into the private sector markets perhaps sooner than we had expected," Acting Council Chair Charlene Drew Jarvis told Reuters.

Also on Tuesday, the city council and Clinton Administration officials moved closer to agreement on a joint memorandum of understanding that would serve as foundation for the White House's proposed financial revitalization plan for D.C., a key D.C. council member said.
Jarvis said following the closed meeting with Office of Management and Budget officials, "I am much more confident now that the council will authorize me to sign an MOU no later than May 6."
She said council approval is likely after Administration officials agreed not to require the city to cede all local authority to write criminal justice laws for felons to the federal government.

Meanwhile, the council's proposed fiscal 1998 budget would provide $17 million more in public school funding than proposed by Barry and $22 million more in police department funding, including a 10 percent pay raise, Jarvis said.

The council rejected the mayor's request for $10 million in economic development funds for areas East of the Anacostia River. And it reduced the city employment services by $8.8 million and human services by $16 million, Jarvis said.
Congress's law creating the control board requires the city to balance its budget in fiscal 1999. The budget cleared by the council on Tuesday would balance the budget in fiscal 1998.
